---
title: "JQI_PersonalFinance_Race"
output: html_document
---

```{r Step 1, include=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# JQI_PersonalFinance_Race.Rmd
#
# Purpose:
# Examine whether the associations between dimensions of
# objective employment quality and personal financial
# satisfaction differ between Black and White respondents.
#
# Primary outcome:
#   financial_satisfaction
#
# Primary predictors:
#   compensation
#   benefits
#   earnings_stability
#
# Primary racial comparison:
#   White vs. Black respondents
#
# Note:
# JQI measures are assigned at the industry-year level.
# Individual-level standard errors should therefore be treated
# as descriptive until an appropriate assignment-level
# inference strategy is established.
# ============================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Setup
# ------------------------------------------------------------

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(fixest)
library(car)
library(broom)
library(modelsummary)

options(scipen = 999)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Load GSS + JQI data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_jq <- readRDS(
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "gss_job_quality_primary_2000_2024.rds"
  )
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Construct financial satisfaction
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# GSS satfin:
#
# 1 = Pretty well satisfied
# 2 = More or less satisfied
# 3 = Not satisfied at all
#
# Reverse-code so that:
#
# 3 = Pretty well satisfied
# 2 = More or less satisfied
# 1 = Not satisfied at all
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_jq <- gss_jq %>%
  mutate(
    satfin_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(satfin)),

    financial_satisfaction = case_when(
      satfin_num == 1 ~ 3,
      satfin_num == 2 ~ 2,
      satfin_num == 3 ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Construct race variable
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# GSS racecen1:
#
# 1 = White
# 2 = Black
#
# Retain only White and Black respondents for the primary
# racial comparison.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_race_jq <- gss_jq %>%
  mutate(
    race_group = case_when(
      racecen1 == 1 ~ "White",
      racecen1 == 2 ~ "Black",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    race_group = factor(
      race_group,
      levels = c("White", "Black")
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Define primary racial analytic sample
# ------------------------------------------------------------

race_satfin <- gss_race_jq %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(race_group),
    !is.na(financial_satisfaction),
    !is.na(compensation),
    !is.na(benefits),
    !is.na(earnings_stability)
  )


# Basic sample description

race_satfin %>%
  count(race_group)


race_satfin %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    years = n_distinct(year),
    industries = n_distinct(industry_common),
    industry_year_cells = n_distinct(
      paste(year, industry_common)
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Distribution of financial satisfaction by race
# ------------------------------------------------------------

race_satfin %>%
  group_by(race_group) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_financial_satisfaction =
      mean(financial_satisfaction, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_financial_satisfaction =
      sd(financial_satisfaction, na.rm = TRUE)
  )


race_satfin %>%
  count(
    race_group,
    financial_satisfaction
  ) %>%
  group_by(race_group) %>%
  mutate(
    percent = 100 * n / sum(n)
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Objective job-quality exposure by race
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Compare the average JQI component values assigned to
# Black and White respondents.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

print(race_satfin %>%
  group_by(race_group) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),

    compensation =
      mean(compensation, na.rm = TRUE),

    benefits =
      mean(benefits, na.rm = TRUE),

    earnings_stability =
      mean(earnings_stability, na.rm = TRUE)
  ))



# Black - White differences

print(race_satfin %>%
  group_by(race_group) %>%
  summarise(
    compensation =
      mean(compensation, na.rm = TRUE),

    benefits =
      mean(benefits, na.rm = TRUE),

    earnings_stability =
      mean(earnings_stability, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    compensation_black_white =
      compensation[race_group == "Black"] -
      compensation[race_group == "White"],

    benefits_black_white =
      benefits[race_group == "Black"] -
      benefits[race_group == "White"],

    earnings_stability_black_white =
      earnings_stability[race_group == "Black"] -
      earnings_stability[race_group == "White"]
  ))


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Unadjusted Black-White difference in financial
#    satisfaction
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_fin_race <- lm(
  financial_satisfaction ~ race_group,
  data = race_satfin
)

summary(m_fin_race)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Separate race-interaction models
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# These models ask whether the association between each
# component and financial satisfaction differs between
# Black and White respondents.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_fin_compensation_race <- lm(
  financial_satisfaction ~
    compensation * race_group,
  data = race_satfin
)

m_fin_benefits_race <- lm(
  financial_satisfaction ~
    benefits * race_group,
  data = race_satfin
)

m_fin_earnings_stability_race <- lm(
  financial_satisfaction ~
    earnings_stability * race_group,
  data = race_satfin
)


summary(m_fin_compensation_race)
summary(m_fin_benefits_race)
summary(m_fin_earnings_stability_race)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Extract racial interaction estimates
# ------------------------------------------------------------

race_interactions <- bind_rows(

  tidy(m_fin_compensation_race) %>%
    filter(term == "compensation:race_groupBlack") %>%
    mutate(component = "Compensation"),

  tidy(m_fin_benefits_race) %>%
    filter(term == "race_groupBlack:benefits") %>%
    mutate(component = "Benefits"),

  tidy(m_fin_earnings_stability_race) %>%
    filter(term == "race_groupBlack:earnings_stability") %>%
    mutate(component = "Earnings stability")

) %>%
  select(
    component,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value
  )


race_interactions


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. Fully joint race × component model
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_fin_components_race <- lm(
  financial_satisfaction ~
    compensation * race_group +
    benefits * race_group +
    earnings_stability * race_group,
  data = race_satfin
)

summary(m_fin_components_race)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 12. Joint test of racial differences across all three
#     components
# ------------------------------------------------------------

race_interaction_terms <- grep(
  "compensation:race_group|race_group.*:benefits|race_group.*:earnings_stability",
  names(coef(m_fin_components_race)),
  value = TRUE
)

race_interaction_terms


linearHypothesis(
  m_fin_components_race,
  race_interaction_terms
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 13. Check multicollinearity
# ------------------------------------------------------------

vif(m_fin_components_race)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 14. Year-specific racial interaction models
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Estimate the three-way structure separately by year:
#
# financial satisfaction ~
#   compensation * race +
#   benefits * race +
#   earnings stability * race
#
# This allows us to see whether racial differences in the
# component relationships are concentrated in particular years.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

yearly_fin_race_models <- race_satfin %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(
    model = map(
      data,
      ~ lm(
        financial_satisfaction ~
          compensation * race_group +
          benefits * race_group +
          earnings_stability * race_group,
        data = .x
      )
    ),
    results = map(
      model,
      ~ tidy(.x)
    )
  ) %>%
  unnest(results) %>%
  filter(
    str_detect(
      term,
      "race_groupBlack"
    )
  )


yearly_fin_race_models %>%
  select(
    year,
    term,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)

m_fin_components_race_year <- lm(
  financial_satisfaction ~
    compensation * race_group * factor(year) +
    benefits * race_group * factor(year) +
    earnings_stability * race_group * factor(year),
  data = race_satfin
)

m_fin_components_race_no3way <- lm(
  financial_satisfaction ~
    compensation * race_group +
    benefits * race_group +
    earnings_stability * race_group +
    compensation * factor(year) +
    benefits * factor(year) +
    earnings_stability * factor(year) +
    race_group * factor(year),
  data = race_satfin
)

anova(
  m_fin_components_race_no3way,
  m_fin_components_race_year
)


# ============================================================
# Predicted Financial Satisfaction by Earnings Stability and Race
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create prediction grid
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Use the observed range of earnings stability in the analysis sample
earnings_range <- seq(
  min(race_satfin$earnings_stability, na.rm = TRUE),
  max(race_satfin$earnings_stability, na.rm = TRUE),
  length.out = 100
)

prediction_grid <- expand_grid(
  earnings_stability = earnings_range,
  race_group = factor(
    c("White", "Black"),
    levels = levels(race_satfin$race_group)
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    # Hold the other two job-quality dimensions at their
    # observed sample means
    compensation = mean(
      race_satfin$compensation,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    benefits = mean(
      race_satfin$benefits,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Generate predicted values and confidence intervals
# ------------------------------------------------------------

predictions <- predict(
  m_fin_components_race,
  newdata = prediction_grid,
  interval = "confidence"
)

prediction_grid <- prediction_grid %>%
  bind_cols(
    as.data.frame(predictions) %>%
      rename(
        predicted = fit,
        conf_low = lwr,
        conf_high = upr
      )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_earnings_race <- ggplot(
  prediction_grid,
  aes(
    x = earnings_stability,
    y = predicted,
    group = race_group,
    linetype = race_group
  )
) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = conf_low,
      ymax = conf_high,
      fill = race_group
    ),
    alpha = 0.15,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Earnings Stability and Satisfaction with Personal Finances",
    subtitle = "Predicted financial satisfaction by race",
    x = "Objective earnings stability",
    y = "Predicted financial satisfaction",
    linetype = "Race",
    fill = "Race",
    caption = "Predictions hold compensation and benefits at their sample means."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray30"),
    plot.caption = element_text(
      hjust = 0,
      color = "gray40"
    )
  )

# Display
p_earnings_race

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Save figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggsave(
  filename = here(
    "04_figures",
    "Financial_Satisfaction_Earnings_Stability_Race.png"
  ),
  plot = p_earnings_race,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 15. Save primary model objects
# ------------------------------------------------------------

saveRDS(
  m_fin_race,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "model_financial_satisfaction_race.rds"
  )
)

saveRDS(
  m_fin_components_race,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "model_financial_satisfaction_components_race.rds"
  )
)
```
